name: HMHS Britannic

sources.title: HMHS Britannic — the third Olympic-class ship, length 269 m, beam 28.65 m; hospital ship; sunk by a mine on 21 November 1916 in the Kea Channel; the wreck on her starboard side at about 120 m
Britannica — Britannic: the wreck at some 119 m, intact except for a large hole in its bow
Hydro International (2008) — Ghostly images of HMHS Britannic: side-scan sonar of the wreck and of the funnels away from it, the nearest about 50 m off
Advanced Diver Magazine — HMHS Britannic, Titanic's sister: the huge hole beneath the forward well deck; the gantry davits; the port ones standing, the starboard ones partly crushed
Divernet — The truth about the Britannic wreck: the bow damaged when it hit the seabed, the ship being longer than the water was deep
RMS Titanic — the sister ship whose hull and superstructure the model shares

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q215692_britannic.py, which shares the Olympic-class hull and superstructure with Q25173_titanic.py; tools/meshkit.py, tools/dresskit.py) with AI assistance. The wreck lies on her starboard side, nearly whole: the bow crumpled, shortened and bent where it hit the bottom first, a large hole beneath the forward well deck, the four funnels torn off and lying flattened 50–90 m from the hull, the gantry davits standing on the port side (uppermost) and partly crushed on the starboard side, torn funnel bases on the boat deck. Dressed with tools/dresskit.py: its own sediment (painted by Offlined with the seabed colour), rust, plates and bottles, textures and baked light. model_built.glb: His Majesty's Hospital Ship as she sailed in 1916 — white hull with a green band and three red crosses a side, buff funnels with black tops, the gantry davits. Approximate: the heading, the exact places of the funnels and of the debris, the number and places of the gantry davits, the internal differences from the Titanic (not modelled). No marine life in the model: Offlined draws the living things itself.
